A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, despite the revised title and NAS-to-MONA rename. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison; localized reporting inconsistencies do not prevent matching the work.

before.justification: v1 reports original instruction-tuning experiments, layer and selection-ratio analyses, LLM-assigned data-quality scores, and physics knowledge-recall results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds larger-model evaluations, additional comparators, activation visualizations and component ablations.

M1.justification: NAS is renamed MONA, but the procedure retains SAE TopK activations, token averaging, an averaged target prototype and generalized Jaccard ranking. Maximizing similarity replaces minimizing one minus similarity, which selects equivalently. Length normalization was already present in v1 Equation 8; its new analysis does not establish a method modification.

E1.justification: OpenHermes-2.5, LESS, the six target benchmarks and the physics knowledge-recall task are retained. v2 adds GPT-4o-generated instruction data through the TyDiQA self-instruct comparison in Appendix D.4, providing a limited additional training-data source without adding a target benchmark or domain.

E2.justification: The established selection baselines remain. v2 adds LLM2Vec to the main comparisons in Tables 1–2 and GPT-4o Self-Instruct to a separate TyDiQA comparison in Table 6. These are bounded extensions of the existing comparison suite.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaMA2-13B evaluation and controlled settings for sparsity, similarity metrics, aggregation and activation extraction. The reported MBPP protocol changes from one shot in v1 Table 2 to three shots in v2 Table 3, without establishing that retained results were rerun. Table 9's OpenHermes-2.5 caption conflicts with Figure 3's LESS setting, so it does not reliably establish another source-dataset change.

E4.justification: v2 adds polysemantic-versus-monosemantic activation comparisons, Math/Code activation visualizations, sparsity and similarity-metric ablations, similar-versus-dissimilar selection controls, and length-normalization analysis. These directly examine previously under-tested design choices. The earlier layer analysis, LLM-analyst case study and physics recall analysis are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions average the random-selection baseline over three seeds. Neither introduces confidence intervals, significance tests, uncertainty bars or a broader repeated-run reporting practice. Individual activation traces in v2 Figure 4 are sample visualizations, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for LLaMA2-13B, LLM2Vec, Self-Instruct and component analyses; Table 2 reports a MONA average of 46.65 for 5% OpenHermes-2.5 selection. Most matched Table 1 values remain unchanged. The OLMo-7B DLRDS-BGE GPQA entry changes from 23.97 to 23.88, and its average from 31.85 to 31.83. New appendix tables also disclose task-level results underlying retained plots.

T1.justification: Appendix D.5 adds a localized approximate derivation of length bias under sum aggregation, using nonnegative activations and magnitude-scaling assumptions, followed by a normalization argument. Section 2.1 also corrects the optimization expression to depend on candidate subset D and distinguishes the target task from its representative examples. No general performance theorem is added.

C1.justification: The central claims of activation-based task-specific selection and improved effectiveness and robustness remain. v2 sharpens the contribution around model-centric, monosemantic representations and withdraws v1's categorical first-use claim for SAE-based selection by acknowledging concurrent work. The rename and expanded abstract do not themselves constitute a new algorithmic contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations concerning activation overlap, length bias, poorer selection at 10%, and possible redundancy in synthesized data. Its limitations replace the claim of easy extension to other training stages with an untested-extension qualification and add the text-only boundary. However, it removes v1's warning that greedy selection ignores diversity while Appendix D.4 describes MONA's selected data as more diverse.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents GPU types, concrete input formats, BGE chunking and pooling for long inputs, the LLM2Vec checkpoint, polysemantic activation extraction, and algorithm pseudocode. These supplement already reported training hyperparameters and SAE access information; BGE processing details do not establish that existing experiments changed. Both versions still describe code release as future work.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning around data-centric versus model-centric representations and acknowledges Yang et al.'s concurrent diversity-driven SAE selection, replacing v1's first-use positioning with a semantic-relatedness distinction. It also adds relevant literature on LLM2Vec, domain shift, sparse coding, CATS and Self-Instruct. This changes the novelty argument beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodological explanations and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten. NAS becomes MONA, experiments are reorganized around explicit research questions, visualization and ablation sections are introduced, and retained supplementary material is redistributed into an expanded appendix structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. Figure 1 is substantially redesigned, the workflow is revised, selection-ratio lines become grouped bars, and activation visualizations and a combined ablation figure are added. Tables gain method groupings and ranking emphasis, with new result tables and relocated retained case-study and prompt displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support for the unchanged method by directly testing activation decomposition, similarity metrics, sparsity and normalization, addressing v1's limited validation of these central choices. Larger-model evaluation, LLM2Vec comparisons and revised novelty positioning further improve the paper. The unexplained MBPP shot change, conflicting Table 9 caption, under-documented Self-Instruct comparison and removed diversity caveat weaken particular claims, but the added component evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
